subject: Calculation invoked from Shiny taking very long to execute

messages.author: 4245924341146ca2
messages.subject: Calculation invoked from Shiny taking very long to execute
parts:
I'm running Shiny locally under Rstudio on an iMac with Safari as the default browser.

I have a function (defined in the global environment) that takes a few milliseconds to execute when directly invoked from the Rstudio console.

However, when I call that same function from within Shiny, it takes about a thousand times longer to complete, and while it is running, the activity monitor shows that one of my cores is running at 100% with Rstudio is the big user.

Any suggestions as to the cause of this behavior?

messages.subject: Re: Calculation invoked from Shiny taking very long to execute
parts:
I'm away from my computer at the moment, but I have determined the cause of the problem. When I pass parameters to the function from the console, they are all 'atomic'. But in the call from Shiny, the parameters are elements from a data frame. I'm now guessing that that was causing coercions that took a lot of time. Now that I am more careful in dealing with the parameters passed in the call from Shiny, the execution time is back to normal. 

BTW, I find Shiny to be wonderfully useful!  Congrats. 

Sent from my iPhone

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Calculation invoked from Shiny taking very long to execute
parts: Oh, OK. If you mean that you are accessing input$foo style variables very often, then that makes sense--those calls will be very expensive indeed. There's actually a fair bit of code that needs to execute when you call input$foo (for reactivity to work, we have to do some accounting whenever you read a reactive variable).
